meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale, and a client call at 4:40. Owen's zero went into the gradebook and he found out on his phone, in class. Start by telling me why nobody called me first.
I didn't come to be thanked, Hale. I asked you a question: why did nobody call me before that zero was entered?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me, Hale. I've done this for twenty years. I asked why nobody called me, and I'm still waiting for an answer.
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
That's twice you've led me, Hale, and I'm not answering questions about Owen's October. What document do you have, and why did the zero go in before anyone called me?
So it's at least possible he used it once?
I don't answer hypotheticals about my son, Hale. He told me he wrote that essay, and you still haven't put one document in front of me.
I agreed to nothing, Hale, and I'm writing down that you said I did. Show me a document or withdraw the zero.
